history.value: Y Combinator was founded in 2005 in Cambridge, Massachusetts by Paul Graham, Jessica Livingston, Robert Morris and Trevor Blackwell, and invented the batch model of startup funding. It funded Airbnb, Stripe, Coinbase, DoorDash, Instacart, Reddit and Dropbox at their start. Led by Garry Tan since 2023, it runs four batches a year from San Francisco and has funded over 5,000 companies.

(meta description). PRO-147: the thesis is the firm's own crisp statement (Erik, 2026-09-26). Published inside quotation marks, as the firm's own words (Erik, 2026-09-26).

investment_stage.basis: Pre-Seed, by Erik's ruling of 2026-09-19: a programme investment on standard terms is a Pre-Seed entry, and YC 'is actually a preseed investor', so S2A does not apply to it. 6,405 of the nameable rows enter at Pre-Seed on the programme terms. The two Growth rows (Convoy, Monzo) are YC Continuity rounds from a growth fund wound back in March 2023, so they do not describe where YC invests today. investment_range.basis: NOT a range in the sense the other firms use, and recorded as the fixed instrument it is: YC invests $500,000 per company — $125,000 for 7% on a post-money SAFE plus $375,000 on an uncapped SAFE with an MFN — identically for every company it accepts, so lower, median and upper are the same number. The Form D entry-round median that the other profiles compute is meaningless for an accelerator and is deliberately NOT computed. Historical progression, all from YC's own posts: ~$6,000 per founder (2005-06), $5,000 + $5,000 per founder (2007-09), $11,000 + $3,000 per founder plus an outside note (2010-14), $120,000 for 7% (Apr 2014), $150,000 for 7% (from W19), $125,000 for 7% (from W21), and the $500,000 structure from Jan 2022. YC Continuity separately wrote growth cheques up to ~$144M (Monzo's Series F), but that vehicle was wound back in 2023 and its cheques are not the firm's current instrument.

funds.basis: All 19 private funds reported in Section 7.B(1) of the ADV, with their sworn gross asset values. Vintages are null: the ADV does not carry them and Form D is not a reliable substitute here — YC's vehicles file 'Indefinite' offerings. FOUR of these funds appear in the ADV and NOWHERE in EDGAR (Y Combinator Fund I and II, YCVC Fund I, YCVC W14), so a Form D sweep alone would have missed them. Conversely the batch vehicles file real numbers: Y Combinator ES24, LLC sold $152,698,436 and ES26 sold $228,321,282, which is better than the accelerator structure was assumed to support.

hq_location.basis: The firm's own site disagrees with the Form ADV principal office, 335 Pioneer Way, Mountain View, CA (Y COMBINATOR, CRD 171730, Annual Amendment filed 2026-03-27). YC's home page says each batch moves to San Francisco for three months and calls Mountain View "the original YC office"; its about page puts the weekly batch meetups in San Francisco. The site names no street address, so this statement is recorded by hand. The Form ADV lists that office (560 20th Street) with 10 advisory staff. Rule (Erik 2026-09-24): the newest Form ADV principal office, unless the firm's own site disagrees, and then the site wins.
